54.0.0.en: 1 “Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD. 2 Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes; 3 For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left; and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited.

54.0.1.en: “Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD” [1].

54.0.2.en: Origen sees that the husband here is the Law, to which the ancient people were bound as to a husband, and it was fitting for her to bring forth abundant fruit, while the Gentiles were deprived of it; yet when they were united with the Lord Christ through faith in Him, they bore children holy to the Lord.

54.0.3.en: St. Augustine compares the Church of the Old Testament with the Church of the New Testament: the first was married to the Law, so that she and her children were in bondage, because she sought temporal blessings; but the second worships God for His own sake, that He may be all in all, and her service is free, belonging to the children of the free woman, not of the bondwoman. The latter was formerly barren and had no children, but now she has many children, more than the first had... This gives her joy and singing.

54.0.4.en: What we say of the Church of the New Testament as a whole we say of every soul that is joined to her, for however barren and dry our past life may have been, the Lord’s wide mercies are able to grant us spiritual fruits of the soul (sons) and of the body (daughters), by our accepting the Cross and enjoying the resurrection with Him.

54.0.5.en: * The Law came to work to make men righteous, but it could not; so (Christ) came and opened the way of righteousness by faith, and in this He accomplished what the Law desired. What the Law could not accomplish by the letter, He accomplished by faith.

54.0.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * The Church extends to the right and to the left, and no longer remembers the shame of her widowhood.

54.0.7.en: * Jerusalem was called, but the first Jerusalem refused to listen, so it was said to her: “Behold, your house is left unto you desolate” (Mt 23:38). But she of whom it is written: “Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear”... did not despise Him who called her. He sends her rain and gives her fruit...

54.0.8.en: After His resurrection He called the Church from all the world, so that she is no longer weak on the Cross but strong in heaven.

54.0.9.en: * That prophecy is fulfilled in which Isaiah speaks through Your tongue to Your Church, Your holy city, the barren one who has children and who is desolate more than she who has a husband. For it was truly said to her: “Rejoice, O barren, thou that didst not bear”... more than the Jewish nation, which has a husband in having received the Law, and more than she who has a visible king. For Your King is hidden, and you have many children from the hidden Bridegroom.

54.0.10.en: St. Augustine What is the result of this fruitfulness?

54.1.0.en: a. “Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes; for thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left; and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited” [2-3].

54.1.1.en: The prophet looked upon the Church of the New Testament as a tent of meeting with the Lord, to which innumerable multitudes would come from the right (the Jews) and from the left (the Gentiles) in an unceasing flood, until the place became very narrow, so he asked for the place of the tent to be enlarged, the curtains made for it to be stretched forth and its cords to be lengthened... For she extends so that the earth may become the Lord’s and His Christ’s; she turns pagan nations into sanctuaries for the Lord, and makes desolate cities into holy dwellings for the people of God.

54.1.2.en: This is the image of the soul that meets the Cross: it truly becomes the tent of the Lord, whose heart widens day by day to bear the image of the Savior, the Lover of mankind. It opens its depths to the good (those on the right) and to the bad (those on the left), so as to embrace in love every soul into a life of fellowship with God in His Son by the Holy Spirit. It is as though the fruitful work of the Cross is the pouring out of the Spirit of love in us, that we may share the love of the Crucified One; we spread the arms of our hearts to embrace all, that His divine saying may be fulfilled in us: “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (Jn 13:35).

54.1.3.en: If the Cross has opened the doors of hope before all nations by divine love, our witness to the Crucified One will not be realized so long as the tent of our hearts is narrow, its doors closed, its cords short and its stakes loose... Let us give our hearts to the Crucified One, and He will establish them as the kingdom of His love, wide enough for all humanity and ever growing!

54.1.4.en: Often we judge others as desolate cities, when it was fitting for us to judge ourselves, because we have not borne in us the love of the Crucified One, which inhabits the desolate cities!

54.1.5.en: * It is not fitting for a man to care for himself only; he must care for others also... For what use is a lamp that does not shine for those sitting in darkness?! And what profit is a Christian who benefits no one else and brings no one back to virtue?!

54.2.0.en: 4 Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more. 5 For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. 6 For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God. 7 For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. 8 In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer. 9 For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee. 10 For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.

54.2.1.en: If the Cross is a shame, a stumblingblock to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles (1 Cor 1:23), yet we bear its fruit and so perceive it as “the power of God, and the wisdom of God,” and we are not ashamed of it (Gal 6:14). Therefore the prophet says: “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more” [4]. At the Cross the soul meets her Bridegroom, the Giver of life, the Conqueror of death, and she forgets her former widowhood and the shame of her youth, for she lived a long time as one alone and forsaken, with no one to fill the void of her heart. Her gazing upon the crucified Bridegroom satisfies all her inner depths, so she cares nothing for the mockery of the daughters of Jerusalem who reject salvation, but in the power of love she says: “I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please” (Song 3:5).

54.2.2.en: St. John Chrysostom relates to us a dialogue between the heavenly Bridegroom and the human soul, in which he says:

54.2.3.en: [Great is my dowry...! He came and took me, and appointed a dowry for me, saying: I give you my riches!

54.2.4.en: Have you lost Paradise? I restore it to you...

54.2.5.en: And yet He did not give me the whole dowry here; why?

54.2.6.en: So that I may give it to you when you enter the royal place.

54.2.7.en: Did you come to Me? No, it is I who came to you... not that you should remain in your place, but that I might take you with Me and return with you. So do not ask Me for the dowry while you are here in this life, but be full of hope and faith.]

54.3.0.en: This is the secret of our joy, and this is the place of our unceasing praise. The Cross has turned our widowhood into a unique wedding in which we are united with the Lord Himself, “For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God” [5-6].

54.3.1.en: We were in shame like a woman whose husband had forsaken her, so that her spirit was broken with shame and disgrace; he refused her because of her adultery and her abominations, and behold, she becomes a bride of the LORD of hosts, the Holy One of Israel, the God of the whole earth, Jesus Christ.

54.4.0.en: When she meets her Bridegroom and enjoys His glories, she forgets the period of her widowhood with all its bitterness, and reckons the whole past as less than a moment or the twinkling of an eye. The grace of the Lord of glory and His kindnesses, which make us one with Him and unite us with His Father, make us perceive with joy His words to us: “For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer” [7-8].

54.4.1.en: Before the eternal mercies of God we count all the days of our affliction as like a small moment that passed so that we might enter the heavenly glories. As for His saying “I will gather thee,” it means the gathering of the holy Church together from all nations, peoples and tongues as one body to the Head, or as one bride to her heavenly Bridegroom. Also in her the believers are gathered together, all the men of the Old Testament with the men of the New Testament; in her the heavenly are gathered with the earthly, and the priests with the people, and so on... All this will not be accomplished unless man is gathered together with himself as a whole, where the soul is subject together with the body with all its senses and feelings, and the mind with the heart and the gifts, and so on... so that he becomes wholly holy to the Lord.

54.5.0.en: This marital love between Christ and the human soul is eternal and does not pass away; for just as God gave Noah a promise that He would not drown the world with a flood in His wrath against mankind [9], so the Lord gives us a promise that He will never leave us or take away His mercy from us, saying: “For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee” [10].

54.5.1.en: In short, He chose us as a bride for Himself, taking away the shame of our widowhood, confirming His love for us and His mercy upon us, giving us sure promises, ever renewed and eternal. He raised us up from the house of adultery, and washed us and sanctified us as a bride for Himself, to bring us into His heavens as a queen sitting at His right hand. And as St. John Chrysostom says: [God desires the adulteress, so what does He do? He does not lead her on high while she is an adulteress, for He does not want to bring her into heaven in this condition, but He came down to her. He came down to earth since she was unable to go up on high. He came to the adulteress and was not ashamed to take hold of her while she was in her drunkenness...].

54.6.0.en: 11 “O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. 12 And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones. 13 And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

54.6.1.en: The secret of our praise is that we were like a barren woman to whom God gave a multitude of children, and like a desolate, forsaken woman who found the Lord Himself as a bridegroom for her, and also like a ruined city which the Lord renewed and rebuilt.

54.6.2.en: “O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones” [11-12].

54.6.3.en: What a wonderful picture it is that reveals the degradation to which humanity had sunk and the surpassing glory, beyond utterance, that has come upon it! It was like a ruined, demolished city, counted in humiliation, and disturbance came upon it through the enemy who took its people captive and made them lose all hope, so that they were without comfort. Now the Lord builds it up in this way:

54.6.4.en: a. He builds its stones with antimony, a sign of strength and firmness. These stones are the souls that accepted faith in the Savior and became living stones in the temple of the Lord, which the enemy of good cannot shatter or snatch away!

54.6.5.en: b. The foundation is of blue sapphire. The foundation is our heavenly (blue) Lord Jesus, the cornerstone who gathers all together in Him.

54.6.6.en: c. The pinnacles of translucent ruby are a reference to the believer’s inner glory, which rests on the righteousness of Christ and the holy life in Him, and is reflected on the outer pinnacles.

54.6.7.en: d. The gates of carbuncle stones point to the sanctification of the senses and our care for them, without shattering them or making light of them.

54.6.8.en: e. All the borders of precious stones point to the complete sanctification of the soul together with the body.

54.7.0.en: f. All her inhabitants are counted disciples of the Lord, and her children are full of peace [13], for the faithful members of the Church are made disciples at the hands of the Lord Himself through her, and every priest or teacher disappears before them, that they may see the Lord Himself working in all. And as St. John Chrysostom says: [Behold the honor of faith: it is not from men nor from man, but by God that they learn this...! The sonship here does not mean “all” (all thy children shall be taught of the LORD) in an absolute way, but means all who have the will. For the teacher sits ready to give what he has to all and to pour out his teaching for all]. And St. Augustine says of the grace of being taught by God: [This grace is called “teaching,” for God teaches those whom He calls according to His purpose, giving them to know what they ought to do, and at the same time to do what they know]. It is as though being taught by God, as a divine gift, has two complementary sides: true spiritual knowledge, and the enjoyment of working and practicing this knowledge in our daily life. He grants us to know the truth and to live it in Him!

54.7.1.en: Through this discipleship the children of the Church enjoy a surpassing peace: “and great shall be the peace of thy children” [13].

54.7.2.en: By sitting at the feet of the Savior we hear His voice and enjoy His resources so as to practice the truth in Him; He grants us the inner peace of the Spirit as a special gift for His children.

54.7.3.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic described St. Anthony after he had spent a period in his severe asceticism, saying: [His body did not change... the disposition of his soul also was blameless, for his soul was not constrained as by grief, nor sunk in pleasure, nor affected by laughter or despair].

54.7.4.en: * Peace is the inheritance that the Lord promised His disciples before His crucifixion... saying: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.” Whoever wishes to be an heir of the Lord Christ, let him reign over the peace of Christ and dwell in it.

54.8.0.en: St. Augustine g. The secret of the Church’s abundant peace, her edification and her strength is the righteousness of Christ, for He says: “In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression; for thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee” [14]. The Apostle says: “Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification” (Rom 4:25).

54.9.0.en: 14 In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression; for thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee. 15 Behold, they shall surely gather together, but not by me: whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall for thy sake. 16 Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. 17 No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD.

54.9.1.en: How it gladdens the heart of the Church which the Lord Himself built and chose as a bride for Himself and a heavenly queen, making her children His disciples at His hands, granting them His surpassing peace, giving them His righteousness and working in them that they may live in righteousness and reject all evil and injustice; yet at the same time she is resisted by the powers of darkness gathered together, and the Lord gives her victory over them and triumph even over death.

54.10.0.en: a. The union of the powers of darkness against her: “Behold, they shall surely gather together, but not by me” [15]... They take counsel and work together against the Church of Christ, as the powers of evil gathered before seeking the crucifixion of her Bridegroom, so that their injustice was turned into salvation for the world, and God brought forth out of the eater meat, and out of the strong sweetness.

54.10.1.en: b. Their being united together makes them fall under the feet of the Church: “whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall for thy sake” [15].

54.11.0.en: c. Their gathering is by divine permission: “I have created the waster to destroy” [16]; therefore we do not fear him nor are we disturbed by the severity of his violence, for he is held in the hand of the Creator.

54.12.0.en: d. Every resistance will surely come to an end, and the Church will be crowned to receive an eternal inheritance of righteousness: “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD” [17].
